scope: All 37 standardized sequence pairs inspected at 22/44 px beside Dad, including 27 native chancery/roundhand variants, nine historical relation adaptations and the original kurrent z.
findings: Native script alphabets have flowing curves, tapered entries and deliberate pressure contrast. Preserve distinct chancery and roundhand letterforms.
Historical relation variants keep clear bars, waves, diagonal arms and quantity distinctions; kurrent z remains distinct from ordinary script z.
The isolated 0.45-pressure comparison gave little useful improvement relative to semantic precision; no additional transformation adopted.
limits: Native glyph identity and mark attachment have separate automated tests; this is visual acceptance only.
The 561-glyph retained font includes mark and layout closure beyond these 37 pairs; this is not all-glyph linguistic validation.
Local outlined specimens do not execute application routing, bidi, balloons or exports.
